- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid missing upward momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often overcorrects downward — raise forecast modestly to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20–25 days) — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for days 25–30 if sentiment is rising.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion — if sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, adjust forecast upward by 0.3–0.8 units for next 3–5 days.  
- Overshoots after sharp spikes (e.g., +3–5% above true) are common — cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above recent peak if sentiment is cooling.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +1.0 → -0.8 → +0.5), model tends to misread trend — apply smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to short-term sentiment swings.
